speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have had a fever and altered mental status for two days; to help me determine the cause, please tell me your age and any other medical conditions you may have.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, could you clarify how you describe the "altered mentation"? Specifically, is it confusion, agitation, or a different change in awareness? Additionally, have you experienced any recent seizures or severe muscle stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use.

The clinical picture of fever, confusion, and generalized rigidity in a patient taking haloperidol is classic for NMS. I will now request specific laboratory results to confirm this.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (including Creatine Kinase), and Liver Function Tests.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (to rule out other causes like encephalitis or stroke).
